שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יִמָּחֲלוּ לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
through whom the entire world will be forgiven.
And now, in the footsteps of Mashiach,
to be aroused to teshuvah in Elul,
as the preparation for the days of Rosh Hashanah,
so that "Hashem is my light" on Rosh Hashanah
"whom shall I fear," etc., "of whom shall I be afraid?" —
for the main fear is of the yetzer hara,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ עַל וְנָתַתִּי שָׁלוֹם בָּאָרֶץ
as we said on "And I will give peace in the land"
אִם אֵין שָׁלוֹם אֵין כְּלוּם וְכוּלֵּי
"If there is no peace, there is nothing," and so on;
is peace from the war of the yetzer hara,
"There is no peace in my bones because of my sin";
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר וְנָתַתִּי שָׁלוֹם בָּאָרֶץ
and about this it says, "And I will give peace in the land,
and you will lie down with none to make you afraid."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And so King David, peace be upon him, sought this,
he who raised up the yoke of teshuvah,
וְלֹא הָיָה דָּוִד רָאוּי לְאוֹתוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה
though David was not fit for that deed,
"and my heart is slain within me,"
for he had already slain the yetzer hara through fasting;
it was only "so that if an individual sinned," and so on
And he said, "Hashem is my shepherd," etc. (Tehillim 23),
"He leads me beside still waters," etc.,
"He guides me in paths of righteousness" —
And this is "Hashem is the stronghold of my life;
of whom shall I be afraid?"
